> Amazon Web Services (which VRChat uses) has lately proven itself to be completely unreliable and a regular interruption to events held in VRChat.

AWS reports no recent issues at https://health.aws.amazon.com/health/status for the past week (or since October 28, 2025 in the North America region, actually). I don't think the issue is with AWS.

The following VRChat status updates are related:

- [Network Connectivity Issues](https://status.vrchat.com/incidents/cm326wdgs2xt) (January 13, 2026)

- [Intermittent slow connection times in the US East region](https://status.vrchat.com/incidents/fjct0f21vl8l) (January 13, 2026)

- [Network Connectivity Issues](https://status.vrchat.com/incidents/k58qfrk1k5hj) (January 14, 2026)

N.B. Epic Games also reports no issues in the past week with Epic Online Services. https://status.epicgames.com/

> Not to mention other hosting providers like Cloudflare and Microsoft Azure have also proven unreliable.

I could not pinpoint the above VRChat issues to a single status page from Cloudflare in the same time period (https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/).

Azure didn't impact VRChat (the last incident on January 10, 2026). https://azure.status.microsoft/en-us/status/history/

The problem is a lot of upstream providers themselves are dependent on AWS US East (definitely EAC, probably others) and if there is service degradation at that one, specific data center, it impacts VRChat even if VRC’s CDN, Networking or API aren’t directly on it. EAC is extremely load-bearing because nothing happens unless it works exactly perfectly with no margin whatsoever, so their reliability is the cap on VRC’s reliability. I’m sure EAC is under pressure to diversify their own upstream providers (*long stare into the camera to emphasize how the previous reasonable statement is certainly not happening*)

details:
Amazon Web Services (which VRChat uses) has lately proven itself to be completely unreliable and a regular interruption to events held in VRChat. I'm part of staff for a weekly DJ music event and it's common for us to have to deal with people dropping out, disconnecting, having to move to a different instance with a different region, etc. While I have no issue with Easy Anti-Cheat and consider it an overall benefit to the platform, EAC has also had issues with failing to authenticate users, which really doesn't help with its already-controversial reputation. Not to mention other hosting providers like Cloudflare and Microsoft Azure have also proven unreliable.

I'd like to suggest a few solutions, as backups for when upstream providers fail:

1) Peer-to-peer connections between players. Obviously not ideal given everyone has different pings, but that's why it's a backup option.

2) Turning the instance owner into a "server" host and having everyone connect to them.

3) Allowing users to set up their own dedicated server linked to a VRChat group, all instances hosted on that server would also be under that group.

In use, these would work the same way as regular VRChat servers, same moderation etc, but not reliant on VRC's flaky upstream providers. They're backups, not replacements.
title: Peer-to-peer or self-hosting to combat unreliable upstream providers
